transcript:
Header:
Date: Dec 14, 2026
Time: 3:00 PM PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Julian Park (Redwood SE); Aisha Khan (NovaHealth Head of ML); Tom Reynolds (NovaHealth CTO); Priya Patel (NovaHealth Infra)
Recording id: ff-20261214-8b7f2c

Summary: Short parity-focused demo to map customer calls from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Walkthrough of API, Console, and Optimize features + Dedicated trial plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, happy to run through the migration parity mapping. I'm Maya Chen, AE on the account, with Julian Park from SE.
[00:08] Julian (Redwood SE): Hey hi, yep, thanks all. Quick check — is the plan still to evaluate both generation paths and embeddings primarily?
[00:15] Aisha (NovaHealth): Yeah that's correct, we're using OpenAI for chat/LLM and Together for a couple of fine-tuned models, plus Anthropic for the safety filter in some pipelines. We want to see parity and cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:28] Tom (NovaHealth): Also want to know about VPC/on-prem options — data residency is a hard requirement for PHI handling.
[00:35] Maya: Totally, we'll show Private/Dedicated options later in the console demo. We'll start high level then dive into the API parity matrix.
[00:42] [01:00] Julian: Ok so first, model mapping. On OpenAI you'd call gpt-4o, or gpt-4o-mini, with temp/top_p. On Redwood the equivalent models are in our catalog — e.g., rwd-4o and rwd-4o-mini — and you can 1:1 set temperature, top_p, max_tokens. We also preserve stop sequences and streaming behavior, though there are some pre-signed differences in how function calling is surfaced, I'll show that.
[01:24] Aisha: When you say preserving streaming, are we gonna see the same chunking behavior? Our realtime chat uses server-sent events today.
[01:31] Julian: We support streaming SSE and we have nearly identical chunk boundaries for the same tokenization, though on quantized models the chunk timings can shift slightly. Our SDKs map streaming to the same events, but sometimes timestamps in logs look a bit different.
[01:48] Priya: And how about KV cache? We currently cache prefixes — will that be compatible?
[01:52] Julian: Yes, we have KV cache support — we call it KV cache in the runtime; sometimes auto-transcribed as K V cash — but it's the same concept: prefix caching to reduce repeated compute. It's automatic for pinned models and configurable per-route.
[02:04] [02:20] Maya: I'll share the parity sheet after the call — mapping of OpenAI params to Redwood: model, temperature, top_p, n, stop, max_tokens, presence_penalty/ frequency_penalty equivalents, embeddings size and encoding notes.
[02:33] Tom: What about function calling differences? We use OpenAI function call to route to microservices.
[02:38] Julian: We support function/tool calling as structured JSON and we also surface a lightweight router in the Console. The big difference is our schema-first validator for functions which can enforce response shapes — helpful for deterministic routing. But developer experience is similar: you send the tools list and the model returns a call object.
[02:55] Aisha: Anthropic has slightly different safety output — we sometimes run the Anthropic classifier post-hoc — can we reproduce that?
[03:02] Julian: We have safety hooks and you can chain models, and Redwood Optimize can run evals against a prompt set to detect regressions vs your Anthropic baseline. We recommend creating a small eval suite and pinning alerts.
[03:16] [03:40] Maya: Now demo time — console. I'll share screen — (brief pause, screen share noise) — top left you see Projects -> NovaHealth Demo. Here are per-route dashboards: tokens, latency p50/p95, cost breakdown by token class.
[03:55] Maya: Here's a route configured to map the OpenAI chat route. Note the 'input_transform' where you can adapt incoming call shape, and the 'model_variant' selector. You can pin to rwd-4o or, for cost-sensitive traffic, rwd-4o-quant.
[04:10] Priya: Is there a way to do canary rollouts? We have to slowly move traffic.
[04:13] Julian: Yup, canary and A/B rollout are first-class: you set traffic weights, and we also support automatic fallback to hosted or lower-cost variants when Dedicated capacity is saturated.
[04:27] [04:45] Tom: For embeddings, we use OpenAI text-embedding-3-small. Are embeddings compatible? Any differences we should expect?
[04:52] Julian: We have a set of Redwood embeddings and they expose the same API shape. There's sometimes small vector distribution differences — we'll run your sample set through both and report cosine similarity numbers. Our Optimize suggestions will recommend quantization or batched calls for throughput.
[05:08] Aisha: Token accounting, though — how do pricing and tokenization align? We bill per token similarly but tokenization details can cause minor deltas.
[05:15] Maya: Right, we'll include a token-breakout sample in the parity sheet. For chargebacks, Console shows per-token cost, and Optimize will show unit-cost improvements per suggestion.
[05:28] [05:45] Priya: Security quick questions: SSO, SAML, audit logs, KMS — do you support customer-managed keys and audit log retention?
[05:52] Maya: Yes — we support SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC at route level, audit logs with exports, and customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations for Private. For Dedicated we can also enable VPC peering and private control plane. We'll attach the SOC2 doc and KMS integration steps.
[06:12] Julian: One note: for on-prem or air-gapped installs, we package an appliance but you lose some of the hosted analytics unless you proxy metrics back — we can walk compliance tradeoffs in the security deep dive.
[06:26] [06:40] Maya: Ok, now quick demo of the API parity curl examples. I'm going to run a sample generation against rwd-4o-mini with temperature 0.2 and stop sequence "\n\n" to mimic your current pipeline.
[06:55] [07:00] (short typing sounds)
[07:04] Maya: Output looks similar, minor differences in phrasing — we'll log the tokens and differences in the parity sheet.
[07:15] Aisha: Any gotchas with streaming vs function calls when you have partial JSON? We sometimes see truncated calls.
[07:22] Julian: Redwood's streaming ensures the call object is emitted as soon as it's recognized; we also have a 'finish_reason' field similar to what you're used to. There are some SDK-level helpers that will reassemble partial messages to avoid truncation.
[07:36] [07:55] Tom: About Dedicated trial — how long to get a sandbox cluster?
[07:59] Maya: We can provision a small Dedicated cluster within 3-5 business days for trials. Julian will provision a cluster for your team, with preloaded models, and run a baseline 1k request throughput/latency bench.
[08:12] Julian: For the benchmark we'll measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens — we'll include cold-start and warmed KV-cache numbers.
[08:24] Priya: Do you expose kernel/runtime traces? We may need to diagnose performance regressions.
[08:28] Julian: Yes we have tracing hooks in Console; you can pull per-request traces and per-model kernel selection logs, though some internal fields are redacted for security.
[08:40] [09:00] Aisha: Ok great. Anything else from Optimize — batching suggestions, quantization?
[09:05] Maya: Redwood Optimize recommended moves: dynamic batching based on latency SLOs, quantization profiles per model that trade quality vs cost, and prefix-KV caching. We'll attach a one-page Optimize runbook.
[09:20] [09:40] Tom: Licensing / pricing — what's the expected delta vs our current spend?
[09:46] Maya: It depends on traffic mix. For many customers we see 15-40% cost reduction with batching + quantized variants, but it depends on embedding volume and long-context generation. We'll run your numbers in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[09:59] Aisha: Any blockers on compliance for PHI?
[10:02] Maya: For PHI we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed KMS and VPC peering; our SOC2 + BA agreement is standard for PHI flows. We'll route legal to finalize.
[10:15] [10:35] Maya: Wrapping up: I'll send the parity matrix and sample curl/SDK snippets; Julian will provision the Dedicated trial and run bench; Aisha will provide prompt set and embedding samples.
[10:47] Tom: Sounds good. Also please include the security whitepaper and SOC2 report link in the next email.
[10:54] Maya: Will do. Any final questions?
[10:58] (silence)
[11:05] Priya: Quick one — do you support per-tenant billing? We need billing separation per BU.
[11:11] Maya: Yes, multi-tenant billing and per-route quotas are supported. We'll include billing docs.
[11:20] [11:40] Maya: Ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items we listed.

End of transcript.

Referenced artifacts: Parity mapping draft, Console screenshots, Security whitepaper, Benchmark spreadsheet.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — some words mis-transcribed (SCO for SSO, K V cash for KV cache), occasional timestamps approximated.
